title: Analytical Psychology
summary: The psyche contains both conscious and unconscious elements organized around archetypes. The Persona is the social mask we present; the Shadow contains what we reject. Individuation is the lifelong process of integrating these parts into a more complete self.
tegBlueUsage: TEG-Blue maps Jung's Persona directly onto the Role Mask — the adaptive presentation developed to navigate social environments. The Shadow contains aspects of the Real Self that had to be suppressed for survival. Integration work in TEG-Blue involves creating safety for suppressed parts to re-emerge.

content.title: Core Concept
content.content: Jung's Analytical Psychology describes the Persona as the social mask we wear — the face we present to the world. It develops through adaptation to social expectations. The Shadow contains everything the ego rejects: traits, desires, and capacities deemed unacceptable. Individuation is the process of integrating Persona and Shadow into a more authentic whole, typically occurring in the second half of life.

content.title: How TEG-Blue Integrates This
content.content: TEG-Blue translates Jung into developmental and regulatory terms. The Persona is the Role Mask — built early, through necessity, not midlife development. The Shadow contains suppressed aspects of the Real Self: emotions, needs, and capacities that weren't safe to express. Integration requires nervous system safety first. The parts in Shadow aren't pathological — they're adaptive suppressions that can re-emerge when conditions change.
